S86.01.needs: a signed-in AGI Cloud account, cloud mode
S86.01.note: Adding or removing sign-in methods other than passkeys is done on the web, not in the app.
steps: Sign in with an AGI Cloud account and open the Profile tab.
Tap "Security and login" in the AGI Cloud section.
Read the "Sign-in methods" group: each linked sign-in appears as a row showing "Last used" or "Linked".
Tap "Passkeys and security keys" and look for "Add a passkey or security key".
Tap "Add or remove a sign-in method" to see that it opens the web security page.
Compare with Expected: password, passkeys and social/SSO identities are all visible, and methods can be added or removed.
S86.01.where: Profile > Security and login > Manage (AGI Cloud section; also Settings > Security and login)

labels.text: Forgot password or try another way

S86.02.needs: an AGI Cloud account that has a password and its current password; an outside sign-in service for reset
S86.02.note: The forgot-password screen in the app only tells the user to visit the website and choose Forgot password; the reset itself is not done in the app.
steps: Open Profile, tap "Security and login" in the AGI Cloud section.
Tap "Change password" (it reads "Set a password" if the account has none).
Fill "Current password", "New password" and "Confirm new password", then tap "Change password" in the sheet.
Read the "Password changed" alert and check that other sessions are signed out.
For a forgotten password, go to the sign-in screen and tap "Forgot password or try another way".
Compare with Expected: change works with the current password; reset is started from the sign-in screen.
S86.02.where: Profile > Security and login > Change password

S86.04.needs: an AGI Cloud account and an authenticator app on a phone
S86.04.note: The section appears only when the server reports two-factor as available or on; the code that asks for the second factor at sign-in was not found in this screen's code.
steps: Open Profile, tap "Security and login", then scroll to "Two-factor sign-in".
Tap "Set up authenticator app" and scan the QR code, or use "Copy setup key".
Type the code from the authenticator app into "Authenticator code" and tap "Turn on".
Check that the "Authenticator app" row now shows on and "Turn off two-factor" appears.
Tap "Turn off two-factor", then "Turn off" in the alert, and check the row goes back to off.
Compare with Expected: turning on makes a code required at sign-in, and it can be turned off.
S86.04.where: Profile > Security and login > Two-factor sign-in

S86.05.needs: an AGI Cloud account with two-factor on
S86.05.note: No control opens the existing codes; they are shown only right after generating new ones, so viewing an old set is not possible in the app.
steps: With two-factor on, open "Security and login" and scroll to "Two-factor sign-in".
Read the "Backup codes" row, which shows "Ready" or "Not set".
Tap "Generate new backup codes" and complete the step-up check if asked.
Tap "Copy codes" or "Save or share" on the codes screen.
Tap "I saved these codes" to finish.
Compare with Expected: codes can be viewed, saved and regenerated.
S86.05.where: Profile > Security and login > Two-factor sign-in > Backup codes

S86.06.needs: an AGI Cloud account with at least one other signed-in session
S86.06.note: The current device row has no tap action, and a row "This device could not be matched to a listed session" appears when the current session is not found; place is not shown in the row text.
steps: Open Profile, tap "Security and login", then scroll to the "Sessions" section.
Read the device rows under "Devices": each shows the device name and a last-active value.
Tap a row that is not this device.
Read the alert "Sign out this device?" and tap "Sign out".
Compare with Expected: the session is listed with device, place and last active, and can be ended.

S86.08.needs: a desktop app already paired by QR code
S86.08.note: Only one desktop card is shown; a browser-to-desktop pairing list was not found in this screen, and the "Remote control" row depends on a feature flag.
steps: Open Settings and tap "AGI Code".
Tap "Remote control" (shown only when the companion feature is on).
On the companion screen, read the desktop card with the "Paired" badge and its name.
Tap "Disconnect" and then "Disconnect" in the alert.
Compare with Expected: the desktop is listed as paired and the pairing can be removed.

labels.text: Log out of AGI Cloud on this device?

S86.09.needs: a signed-in AGI Cloud account, cloud mode
S86.09.note: This signs out only this device; the Log Out row is shown only in cloud mode with a cloud account.
steps: Open the Profile tab in cloud mode while signed in.
Scroll to the "AGI Cloud" section and tap "Log Out".
Read the alert "Log out of AGI Cloud on this device?".
Tap "Cancel" once to check it leaves you signed in, then tap "Log Out" again.
Compare with Expected: the app signs out on this device and returns to sign-in.

S86.10.needs: an AGI Cloud account and a second signed-in device or browser to check
S86.10.note: The app only calls the server action; whether every device credential is revoked is decided on the server and was not verified from the code.
steps: Open Profile, tap "Security and login", then scroll to the "Sessions" section.
Tap "Log out of all devices" (shown in cloud mode only).
Read the alert "Log out of all devices?" and tap "Log out everywhere".
Check that the app returns to sign-in.
Compare with Expected: one action signs out every browser, app and device.
S86.10.where: Profile > Security and login > Sessions > Log out of all devices

steps: Open Settings and tap "Connectors" (cloud mode).
Tap a connector that shows as connected.
Find the "Connected" row and the "Granted access" section.
Scroll to the bottom and tap "Disconnect", then "Disconnect" in the alert.
Compare with Expected: the connector leaves the list, or a notice says it is disconnected.
S86.12.where: Settings > Connectors > tap a connected connector > Disconnect

S86.20.needs: none; a phone with the microphone permission in either state
S86.20.note: The app can only request the permission from the system; a permission already denied may need the iOS Settings app, which was not verified.
steps: Open Settings and tap "Capabilities".
Tap "Camera and files".
Tap "Microphone" in the Permissions list.
Read the status and the level choices shown on the detail screen.
Tap the request button if shown, then compare with Expected: the user sees and can change microphone access.
S86.20.where: Settings > Capabilities > Camera and files > Permissions > Microphone

S86.21.needs: none; a phone with the camera permission in either state
S86.21.note: The app can only request the permission from the system; a permission already denied may need the iOS Settings app, which was not verified.
steps: Open Settings and tap "Capabilities".
Tap "Camera and files".
Tap "Camera" in the Permissions list.
Read the status and the level choices on the detail screen.
Tap the request button if shown, then compare with Expected: the user sees and can change camera access.
S86.21.where: Settings > Capabilities > Camera and files > Permissions > Camera

S86.23.needs: a connected connector that lists tools
S86.23.note: The saved choices are listed per connector only; no single screen lists every saved approval, and removing by setting back to Ask was not verified.
steps: Open Settings and tap "Connectors".
Tap a connected connector.
Scroll to "Tool permissions".
Set a tool to "Allow" or "Block" and reopen the connector.
Check the choice is kept, and set it back to "Ask" to remove the saved choice.
Compare with Expected: saved always-allow and always-deny choices can be reviewed and removed.
S86.23.where: Settings > Connectors > tap a connector > Tool permissions

S86.24.needs: a connected connector to test the approval
S86.24.note: The "Skip approvals" choice is disabled when the workspace does not allow it; Expected names "auto-approve safe", but the middle choice is "Run read-only actions without asking".
steps: Open Settings and tap "Capabilities".
Tap "Action approvals".
Read the three choices: "Ask before every action", "Run read-only actions without asking" and "Skip approvals".
Tap one choice and check that it is marked as selected.
Ask chat to run a connector action and compare what AGI asks before doing it with Expected.

S86.26.needs: an AGI Cloud account, cloud mode
S86.26.note: No control named hardened mode was found; "Lockdown mode" is the closest control, it shows only after its state loads, and "Advanced Account Security" opens a web page.
steps: Open Profile, tap "Security and login".
Scroll to the "Lockdown mode" switch, below "Recent security activity".
Read its description: "Blocks connectors, web access, code execution and Deep Research."
Turn it on, then try a chat that uses web search or running code.
Compare with Expected: stronger limits apply; turn it off again to restore normal use.
S86.26.where: Profile > Security and login > Lockdown mode
